observations: Black freestanding cooker with a glass oven door.
The brand 'POLYSTAR' is printed on the oven door in photo 0.
Six control knobs are visible on the front panel.
The top surface shows one gas burner on the left and one electric hotplate on the right; the rest of the top is obscured.
The unit appears heavily used with visible grime on the front panel and oven glass.
The cooker is positioned between a wall and a chest freezer.

claims.evidence: Only one gas burner is clearly visible in photo 0; the other side of the top is obscured.
Only one electric hotplate is clearly visible in photo 0.
The internal heating elements or gas burners for the oven cannot be confirmed from an external photo.

risks.risk: Gas burners may be clogged, leaking, or have failed auto-ignition.
risks.proof: A video showing all gas burners lit with a steady blue flame.

risks.risk: Electric hotplates may be burnt out or have faulty wiring.
risks.proof: A video showing both electric plates heating up (e.g., boiling a small amount of water).

risks.risk: The oven or grill (gas or electric) may not function.
risks.proof: A video showing the oven interior with the heat source (flame or glowing element) active.

risks.risk: The exterior and interior may have significant rust or permanent staining hidden by the current grime.
risks.proof: Clear photos of the top surface, oven interior, and sides after cleaning.
risks.if_unproven: as requiring deep cleaning and potential repair

proof_requests: Photo of the entire top surface to confirm the 2+2 burner/plate configuration.
Video showing all burners, plates, and the oven functioning.
Photo of the manufacturer's label/sticker (usually on the back or inside the door) for the exact model number.
Photos of the oven interior and the sides of the unit.
response.reason: The item is identified as a Polystar freestanding cooker. Due to the visible grime and lack of operational proof, it is priced at its worst case as a non-functional unit requiring professional cleaning.
